evidence.AC1: POST /todos with {"title":"past","dueDate":"2026-10-01"} returned 201 with dueDate "2026-10-01". POST without dueDate returned 201 with dueDate null. The value is a plain YYYY-MM-DD date, and a datetime string was rejected.
evidence.AC2: PATCH /todos/2 with {"dueDate":"2026-09-15"} returned 200 and the date changed from 2026-12-01 to 2026-09-15. PATCH /todos/4 with a date set it, and PATCH with {"dueDate":null} returned 200 with dueDate null, so it was removed.
evidence.AC3: POST with dueDate "2026-02-30" returned 400. POST with "23.10.2026" returned 400. POST with "2026-10-01T10:00:00Z" returned 400. PATCH with "2026-02-30" returned 400.
evidence.AC4: Today is 2026-10-23. The test data was: past 2026-10-01 (open), future (changed to 2026-09-15, open), today 2026-10-23 (open), none (no date), and donepast 2026-09-01 (done). GET /todos?overdue=true returned only ids 1 and 2. It excluded the todo due today, the todo with no date and the done todo. GET /todos still returned all five.
evidence.AC5: The list page at / showed 'past · Fällig: 2026-10-01', 'future · Fällig: 2026-09-15', 'today · Fällig: 2026-10-23' and 'donepast ✓ · Fällig: 2026-09-01'. The todo without a date showed no due date.
evidence.AC6: In the page snapshot, 'past' and 'future' (both open, due before today) carried '⚠ überfällig'. 'today', 'none' and the done 'donepast' had no such marker.
evidence.AC7: The page has a button 'nur überfällige'. Clicking it reduced the list to just 'past' and 'future', both marked überfällig, and the button text changed to 'alle anzeigen'.
